constraints: Use WEB Get body part count first to learn how many parts are available to parse.
For file parts, contents must be captured into a Blob; for plain Text form fields submitted in a multi-part request, contents can be captured into Text.
mimeType and name are optional but must be passed together: both are received only when the part was submitted as <input type="file">; otherwise both are absent.
_needsReview: Confirmed via the live doc page's rendered HTML that mimeType is paired with name (not fileName) in the 'optional but must be passed together' rule. However the page's own two descriptions of `name` conflict: its parameter tooltip reads 'Name of "input" variable' (i.e. the HTML form field's name attribute), while the surrounding prose sentence reads '...receive the Mime type and the name of the original file' (i.e. same content as fileName). Left name's description following the tooltip/parameter-table gloss (input field name) since that is the more specific, parameter-table-sourced text, but this may actually mean the original file's name -- please verify against a live WEB GET BODY PART example/response.

jointConstraints.rule: Optional together: when the part is a submitted file both are received; otherwise both are absent.

params.name: part
params.description: Number of the part to be parsed.

params.name: contents
params.description: Contents of the part (Blob for files, Text for submitted text fields).

params.name: name
params.description: Name of the HTTP input field (variable name); only present when the part was submitted as <input type="file"> (paired with mimeType). See _needsReview: doc prose alternately suggests this holds the original file's name instead.

params.name: mimeType
params.description: Mime type of the submitted file, if any; only present when the part was submitted as a file (paired with name).

params.name: fileName
params.description: Name of the submitted file, if any; only present when the part was submitted as a file.
